text:
olivia: Heads up — spotted a latency regression in the kernel picker for flash v3 when head_dim is non-multiple-of-8 on SM86. Noticed it while running long seq workloads (seq=1024) against the canary model. p50 jumped ~12% compared to last week.

ben: repro? minimal steps and commit that triggered the picker change?

olivia: repro is simple: run the perf harness on the openai-compat model with head_dim 22/30. Example: `./perf/harness --model rwd/v3-canary --seq 1024 --head-dim 22 --batch 1 --kernel-autotune` My local run id: run-2026-03-17-olivia-07. Attaching profiler snippet below.

olivia: ```
PROFILE run-2026-03-17-olivia-07
arch: sm86
seq: 1024
head_dim: 22
kernel chosen: flashv3_causal_prefetch_unaligned
latency p50: 42.1 ms (baseline 37.5 ms)
CPU dispatch overhead: 0.8 ms
GPU kernel time: 39.7 ms -> 35.2 ms prev
observed: extra mem-copy + prefetch stalls when head_dim % 8 != 0
```

maria: interesting. I remember we added an alignment-aware fastpath in the picker that prefers prefetch variant for v3; looks like the heuristics didn't account for head remap padding when hd%8 != 0. Could be causing additional per-head tile handling (extra memcpy / remap) which kills throughput.

ben: can you dump kernel selection trace for a single request? do we see fallback to slowpath or an extra remap kernel?

olivia: trace snippet (single request): `KERNEL_PICKER: v3 -> prefetched_variant (hd=22) -> remap_kernel` so it chooses prefetch but inserts remap. The remap kernel runs per-head and isn't batched well for odd head counts.

maria: hypothesis: on sm86 the prefetch kernels expect 8-wide head alignment to utilize vectorized ld/st. When hd not aligned, codepath inserts scalar remap leading to many small memops. SM80 used wider vectorization pattern that hid this.

ben: makes sense. Do we have perf counters? L2 misses or shared mem stalls?

olivia: yes - L2 miss rate up ~4x, global load throughput down. Added counters: `gpc_l2_miss` and `inst_eligible_warps` in the snippet above.

perf-bot: nightly-regression: infra/perf/runs/run-2026-03-17-olivia-07 flagged +11.8% latency on p50 for rwd/v3-canary (seq=1024, hd=22). Dashboard: https://perf.internal/runs/run-2026-03-17-olivia-07

maria: quick mitigation options: 1) force kernel picker to prefer the conservative (non-prefetch) v3 slowpath when hd % 8 != 0 on SM86; 2) add a remap fusion that merges remap into prefetch for odd heads (more invasive but better perf); 3) add a small JIT specialization for hd <= 32 odd cases.

ben: I'd vote for (1) as a fast rollback to get canary back to baseline, and queue (2) as a medium-term fix. We should also add tests to the autotuner to exercise odd head dims.

olivia: agree. I've opened a tiny revert patch to the picker heuristics: `revert: prefer_prefetch_on_unaligned=false` and pushed to branch `picker-hotfix/olivia/odd-heads`. Can run a canary if we want.

deploy-bot: canary job scheduled: `canary/picker-hotfix-olivia-2026-03-17` -> rollout window 30m -> notify channel on completion.

ben: after canary, please run the full perf harness (seq 512/1024, hd 22/30/14, sm80/sm86) and post numbers. Also add regression alert suppression for the canary run id (so perf-bot doesn't spam).

olivia: will do. Also adding autotuner unit test to assert kernel picks for hd in [8,16,22,30] on both sm80 and sm86. PR incoming.

maria: for the longer term, I'll sketch a remap-fusion patch and estimate engineering effort. If fusion shows <3% overhead for aligned and gives >10% for odd heads, it's worth it.

olivia: thanks all. Action items: olivia = canary + perf runs + test, ben = validate counters and review picker revert, maria = remap-fusion design doc. Revisit in 24h. :thumbsup:
